text: A circle of radius $1$ is tangent to a circle of radius $2$. The sides of $\triangle ABC$ are tangent to the circles as shown, and the sides $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ are congruent. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
figure: Tall isosceles triangle ABC with apex A at the top and base BC horizontal at the bottom (B left, C right). Two circles are stacked on the vertical line of symmetry: a small circle of radius 1 near the top and a larger circle of radius 2 below it, touching each other. The small circle is tangent to sides AB and AC. The large circle is tangent to sides AB and AC and to the base BC. A vertical radius is drawn in each circle, labeled 1 in the small circle and 2 in the large circle.
